title: Critical Node.js Sandbox Flaw Exposes AI Agents to Host Code Execution
content_md: A critical vulnerability in the Node.js sandboxing library, isolated-vm, has exposed a serious risk to AI agents, automation platforms, and applications that execute untrusted JavaScript. The flaw, tracked as GHSA-864f-rcv7-6rh4, is a type confusion issue that can enable code running inside a sandbox to crash or potentially seize control of the host process. Cris Staicu said the affected package receives more than 1 million downloads per week and is widely used by developers who need to isolate user-supplied or model-generated code. Critical Node.js Sandbox Flaw Fixed releases are available, but organizations relying on earlier versions should treat this as an urgent patching priority. The vulnerability exists in ExternalCopy, a feature that moves serialized values between separate V8 Isolates. An Isolate normally provides a strong boundary: it has its own heap, built-ins, and object graph, so sandboxed code cannot access host resources unless the application intentionally grants a capability. ExternalCopy supports a transferList option for moving ArrayBuffers without copying their underlying memory. During processing, however, isolated-vm validated transfer-list entries during one pass and transferred them in a second pass. An attacker could use a JavaScript getter to return a real ArrayBuffer during validation, then return a different value when native transfer logic ran again.
